title: Through the Day Thy Love Hath Spared Us
description: Through the Day Thy Love Hath Spared Us in Tonic Solfa to KALMAR, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Kelly wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 43.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.7.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to KALMAR; any other 8.7.8.7.7.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Through the day Thy love hath spared us, Now we lay us down to rest; Through the si-lent watch-es guard us, Let no foe our peace mo-lest: Je-sus, Thou our Guar-dian be; Sweet it is to trust in Thee.

lines: Through the day Thy love hath spared us,
Now we lay us down to rest;
Through the silent watches guard us,
Let no foe our peace molest:
Sweet it is to trust in Thee.
Pilgrims here on earth and strangers,
Dwelling in the midst of foes,
Us and ours preserve from dangers;
In Thine arms may we repose
And, when life’s sad day is past,
Rest with Thee in heaven at last.
Triune God, let all adore Thee,
Saints on earth and saints in heav’n;
Who hast all their being giv’n,
Who dost seek and save the lost:

licence: Public domain: Thomas Kelly died in 1855.
credits: Words by Thomas Kelly (1769–1855), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to KALMAR by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
